title: fix(zone.js): zone-node only patch Promise.prototype.then
evidence: issue 50457: Hi @pjms, In both cases the problem is caused by a change in zone.js https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/49144 (//cc @JiaLiPassion).
reason: The fix reverts this change, saying its then-only patching caused several regressions. The change's new `makeResolver` wrapper visibly swallows errors thrown in then-callbacks, a behavioral defect present in its diff.
ground_truth: The new `lib/node/promise.ts`, now used as the `zone-node` entry point, replaces ZoneAwarePromise with a patch of `Promise.prototype.then` only. Its `makeResolver` wraps every onResolve/onReject callback in `zone.runGuarded(() => task.invoke())`. `runGuarded` catches exceptions and passes them to the zone's `onHandleError`. When that hook returns false, as Angular's NgZone does, the exception is swallowed and the wrapper returns `undefined` to the native `then`. So inside NgZone, `p.then(() => { throw err; }).catch(handler)` never reaches `handler`; the chained promise resolves with `undefined` instead of rejecting, breaking error propagation (e.g. in SSR). In addition, native `await` and other engine-internal promise reactions bypass the patched `then`, so they no longer take part in zone tracking the way they did with ZoneAwarePromise. The fix reverted the change and went back to patching the whole Promise (ZoneAwarePromise) in the `zone-node` bundle.

title: fix(zone.js): support `Timeout.refresh` in Node.js
evidence: Found by bench-eval controlcheck: the fix deletes a line this change added.
reason: The change added `data.isRefreshable = isFunction(handleOrId.refresh)` in scheduleTask. That line throws a TypeError when the native timer returns null or undefined, and the fix changes exactly that line.
ground_truth: In `patchTimer`'s `scheduleTask`, the change stores the native timer's return value in `handleOrId`. When it is not a number, it executes `data.isRefreshable = isFunction(handleOrId.refresh)`. Some environments return null or undefined from `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame`, for example a browser extension, policy or automation wrapper that blocks the call. The old code explicitly tolerated a nullish handle. With this change, reading `.refresh` on null throws a TypeError synchronously, so calling the patched `setTimeout` crashes instead of returning. The fix uses optional chaining (`handleOrId?.refresh`) so a nullish handle is treated as non-refreshable.

title: fix(compiler): transform pseudo selectors correctly for the encapsulated view
evidence: issue 58399: I think we can close this as a dupe of #58226 (as you said, it s caused by #57796)
reason: The change reworked selector splitting so that comma lists and combinators inside parentheses stay in one part, and it added another non-newline-safe `/([^:]*)(:*)(.*)/` split. As a result, multiline selectors inside pseudo-functions are now truncated; the issue discussion attributes this regression to this change.
ground_truth: In `ShadowCss._scopeSelector`/`_applySelectorScope`, the change replaced the simple `/ ?, ?/` comma split and the combinator separator with regexes that do not split inside parentheses. A selector part like `.foo:is(.a,\n.b)` therefore now reaches `_scopeSelectorPart` as a single string that can contain newlines. That function splits the part with `/([^:]*)(:*)(.*)/`, both in the newly added pseudo-function `:host` branch (`scopedP.match(...)`) and in the non-host branch (`t.match(...)`). Because `.` does not match a newline, everything after the first newline is silently dropped. For example, a component style `.foo:is(.a,\n.b) {}` is emitted as `.foo[contenta]:is(.a,`, with the rest of the selector and the closing parenthesis lost, which breaks the stylesheet. The fix changed the trailing group of both regexes to `([\s\S]*)` so content after newlines is kept.

title: refactor(devtools): ignore `getInjector` when it is not supported
evidence: git : fix(devtools): handle case where directive metadata has `undefined` dependencies (#60256) This fixes a bug introduced by [#60206](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60206/files#diff-c07b9ecd59f6e0ed636ac9672b9644178d9a999f04bc8b8198b13e86589df
reason: The change makes `metadata.dependencies` conditional on finding an injector. That breaks the previous invariant that it is always set, and the frontend crashes on the undefined value. The fix explicitly attributes the bug to this change.
ground_truth: In `getLatestComponentState` (component-tree.ts), the change wraps `metadata.dependencies = getDependenciesForDirective(...)` in `if (injector)`. Previously `dependencies` was always assigned on the directive metadata. Now `getInjectorFromElementNode` returns null whenever `ng.getInjector` is not supported (or returns nothing), and in that case `dependencies` is left `undefined`. The DevTools property view template evaluates `controller().directiveMetadata?.dependencies.length > 0`. The optional chain only guards `directiveMetadata`, not `dependencies`. So when an app's global `ng` lacks `getInjector`, selecting a component throws a TypeError reading `length` of undefined and the property panel breaks. The fix guards the template by first checking that `dependencies` exists before reading its `length`.

title: refactor(devtools): defer tabs
evidence: git : ols): errors caused by the injector tree (#62029) Errors: - Attempting to translate SVGs when the tab is not on focus (Regression from #61241) - Null injector node focus error Extra: - Improve scoping of the injector-tree component class members PR Close #620
reason: The fix explicitly names this change as the source of the regression where the injector tree tries to translate SVGs while its tab is not shown. The faulty afterRenderEffect and the switch to `[hidden]`/display:none are both introduced in this diff.
ground_truth: This change rewrites `InjectorTreeComponent` to render from an `afterRenderEffect` that runs whenever the `componentExplorerView` input changes. The effect calls `init()` and `updateInjectorTreeVisualization(view.forest)` without checking whether the tab is visible. The change also hides the deferred `ng-injector-tree` with `[hidden]` (display:none) and removes the old `ng-injector-tree.hidden` CSS, which had kept the element laid out with `visibility: hidden`. So once the Injector Tree tab has been opened and the user switches to another tab, every new component explorer view re-runs the effect. D3 then tries to lay out, translate and snap SVG trees inside an element with no layout, which throws errors. `init()` also runs on every effect execution, re-registering the `highlightComponent` listener and recreating the visualizers each time. The fix adds a `hidden` input bound to the host's `[hidden]`, returns early from the effect when it is true (read untracked), and calls `init()` only once, when the visualizers do not exist yet.

title: build: move dependencies on npm package of dev-infra to workspace dependency
evidence: git : fix(devtools): zone.js not being loaded for dev and prod builds (#62239) Fixes a regression from #62083 by updating the remaining script imports. PR Close #62239
reason: The fix explicitly calls this a regression from this change. The BUILD rule edits moved where zone.js lands in the packaged app, but two index.html files still load the old path. As a result the DevTools dev and prod builds ship without zone.js loaded, which is a runtime defect.
ground_truth: The change switches the zone.js dependency in `devtools/src/BUILD.bazel` (the `devapp` pkg_web) and `devtools/projects/shell-browser/src/BUILD.bazel` (the static files filegroup). It goes from `@npm//:node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js` to the workspace target `//:node_modules/zone.js`. That moves the packaged file from `./npm/node_modules/zone.js/...` to `./node_modules/zone.js/...`. The change updated the `<script>` tag only in `demo-standalone/src/index.html`. `devtools/src/index.html` and `devtools/projects/shell-browser/src/index.html` still reference `./npm/node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js`. In both the DevTools dev app and the production browser-extension build, that script 404s and zone.js is never loaded, so the zone-based Angular app fails to bootstrap or run correctly. The fix updated both index.html files to load `./node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js`.
